summary: Verified the shared app-scroll scrollbar style. Chromium computed styles: planning-dialog, planning-delete-dialog, edit-tenant-dialog and planning-calendar all have the app-scroll class. Their ::-webkit-scrollbar is 4px wide and 4px high. ::-webkit-scrollbar-button is display:none with width 0. The Firefox fallback (scrollbar-width/scrollbar-color) is inside @supports not selector(::-webkit-scrollbar), so it does not override the webkit styles in Chrome 121+; computed scrollbar-width in Chromium is auto. planning-calendar has overflow-x auto. Mobile (390x800): the calendar scrolls horizontally (scrollWidth 620 vs clientWidth 324 in week view and 760 vs 324 in bays view). Setting scrollLeft and a horizontal mouse wheel both scroll the calendar, and the page itself has no horizontal overflow. planning-dialog fits the viewport (16 to 784) and scrolls internally (new: 830>766, edit: 982>766). On desktop (1920 and 1024 wide) the calendar fits its container (minWidth 620/760), so there is no overflow to scroll; this is expected. Regression: deleted a converted appointment on mobile. The dialog text says the work order stays intact; after confirming, the event disappears and the DB still has the work order. The backend test test_iter20_appointment_delete.py passes 5/5.

issues: The react-big-calendar toolbar (Astăzi/Înapoi/Înainte and the date label) sits inside the horizontally scrolling app-scroll container. On 390px the 'Înainte' button is clipped and the toolbar scrolls away along with the grid. Optional: let only the grid scroll, or wrap the toolbar.
The today column/slot highlight is light blue (default rbc .rbc-today), which is high-contrast against the dark theme (existing behaviour).
The Actions column of the tenants table is clipped at 1024px (the 'Șterge' button is cut off). If the table wrapper scrolls horizontally, consider applying app-scroll there too for consistency.

critical_code_review_comments: The CSS is correct. The sidebar-scroll and app-scroll selectors are shared, so there is no duplication. The @supports guard correctly avoids the Chrome 121+ standard-property override. The thumb is transparent until hover, so touch users get no visual scroll affordance in dialogs; this matches the requested sidebar behaviour.
